original_question: Determine whether the two theorems cited from [Lo5] continue to hold for broader classes of Jordan pairs: namely, whether PE(V) is perfect exactly when V has no simple factors isomorphic to (F2, F2), (F3, F3), or (H2(F2), H2(F2)), and whether PE(V) is simple exactly when V is simple and avoids those exceptional factors.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1, together with its nearby sharpening/reformulation in Proposition 1.2 and the partial positive evidence in Theorem 1.3, concerning whether Loos's perfectness and simplicity criteria for the projective elementary group PE(V) extend from the class treated in Loos's earlier papers to the generality considered in this survey.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core mathematical content of the paper's target question: it is about extending Loos's criteria for when the projective elementary group PE(V) of a Jordan pair is perfect and when it is simple, and it identifies the same three exceptional simple Jordan pairs that obstruct these properties, namely (F2,F2), (F3,F3), and (H2(F2),H2(F2)). It also keeps the focus on PE(V), not on neighboring issues such as central extensions or presentations of Steinberg groups.
missing_details: The paper's formulation is a definite conjecture/open problem, not just a vague request to test 'broader classes'; the quantifier should be stated explicitly in the same breadth as Conjecture 1.1.
PE(V) should be defined stand-alone as the projective elementary group attached to the Jordan pair V.
The ambient scalar setting is omitted; the paper works with Jordan pairs over its standard commutative unital base ring, so the rewritten question should not read as field-only unless the paper does.
The meaning of 'simple factors' should be made explicit in the stand-alone question, i.e. the relevant simple direct factors in the structural decomposition used by the paper/Loos.
The exceptional object H2(F2) should be identified as the Jordan algebra of 2 x 2 symmetric (hermitian) matrices over F2, viewed as the Jordan pair (H2(F2),H2(F2)).
The simplicity clause needs its full biconditional form: PE(V) is simple if and only if V itself is simple and avoids the three exceptional cases.

Your wording attributes both cited results to '[Lo5]'; the paper's nearby discussion distinguishes the Loos results on perfectness and on simplicity, so the source attribution should follow the paper's citation pattern rather than compress them into one undifferentiated reference.
If the refined question is to be fully stand-alone, F2 and F3 should be read as the finite fields with 2 and 3 elements, respectively.
refined_question: Let V be a Jordan pair over the same commutative unital base ring as in the paper, and let PE(V) denote its projective elementary group. Is it true, as asked in Conjecture 1.1, that the Loos criteria for perfectness and simplicity extend to this full setting: namely, that PE(V) is perfect if and only if V has no simple factor isomorphic to (F2,F2), (F3,F3), or (H2(F2),H2(F2)); and that PE(V) is simple if and only if V is simple and V is not isomorphic to any of these three exceptional Jordan pairs?
justification: The draft is essentially aiming at the paper's opening conjecture about PE(V): the nearby discussion in Section 1 isolates exactly the perfectness and simplicity criteria coming from Loos, packages them as the main open problem, and then follows with Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 as the immediate reformulation/partial supporting result. The refined question therefore stays narrowly with the PE(V) perfect/simple iff-statements and the three exceptional simple Jordan pairs, avoiding drift into other open problems in the survey such as universal central extensions of Steinberg groups or root-graded presentations.
